claim_text: Melatonin may be useful for selected circadian rhythm problems such as jet lag when timing is appropriate, but effects depend on the sleep/circadian indication and administration timing; evidence does not support treating it as a generic solution for chronic insomnia.
health_goal_or_outcome: Differentiate circadian timing indications from chronic insomnia before considering melatonin.

population.age_range: Adults; children and adolescents require separate clinical assessment.
population.sex_or_life_stage: Pregnancy and breastfeeding require clinician review.
population.health_status: People with jet lag or shift-work-related circadian disruption.
population.other_context: Travel direction, time zones, schedule and concomitant medicines matter.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Melatonin supplements; formulation and release profile vary.
evidence_summary: NCCIH Melatonin and Sleep Disorders pages describe evidence limitations, circadian indications and safety considerations.
limitations: No dose or timing protocol established in this claim.
Circadian indications differ from chronic insomnia.
Sedation, interactions and product-quality issues require review.
